speed-ramp.context: A video clip box with a smooth S curve climbing across it from low to high. Used in video editors for speed ramping, slow motion to fast motion transitions and time remapping.

video-stabilization.context: A steady frame in the middle with wobbly lines on both sides, showing shake being removed. Marks stabilise or smooth footage options in video editors and cameras.

earbud-case.context: A pill shaped charging case with its lid open above two earbuds sitting inside. Used for wireless earbud battery status, pairing and charging screens.

neckband-earphones.context: A U shaped flexible neckband with an earbud at each end. Used for Bluetooth neckband headsets, sports earphones and wireless audio accessories.

headphone-stand.context: A pair of over ear headphones resting on an upright stand with a crossbar on top and a flat base. Used for desk setups, audio gear shops and headphone storage or charging dock features.

simulcast.context: A circled play button on the left with branching lines leading to three small screens. Used for streaming to several platforms at once, multi destination broadcasts and simulcast schedules.

intermission.context: Closed stage curtains with a small hourglass in the middle. Used for theatre and cinema interval notices, break screens and paused live events.

vintage-movie-camera.context: An old fashioned film camera on tripod legs with two reels on top, a lens at the front and a hand crank on the side. Used for classic cinema, silent film topics and filmmaking features.

audio-only.context: A dashed video frame with a pair of headphones inside it, meaning the picture is off and only sound plays. Used for audio only playback modes, podcast versions of videos and low data listening.

video-loop.context: A video frame holding a small play triangle wrapped in a circular arrow. Used for repeat playback, looping clips, GIF style videos and autoplay loop settings.

frame-capture.context: A camera shutter aperture inside four corner brackets. Used to grab a still frame from a video, take a screenshot of playback and save a freeze frame.

dvr.context: A flat set top recorder box with a record dot on its front and a small clock display. Used for digital video recorders, scheduled TV recordings and cable box features.

tv-input-source.context: A television with an arrow pointing into its left side. Used for choosing the TV input or source such as HDMI, AV or antenna, and for external input settings.

party-speaker.context: A tall floor speaker with two round woofers and light rays flashing from its top corner. Used for party sound systems, DJ gear and loud portable speaker features.

suitcase-record-player.context: A portable suitcase style record player with its lid open, a turntable platter and a tone arm. Used for vinyl, retro audio and portable turntable topics.

cassette-adapter.context: A cassette tape with a thin cable leaving its edge and ending in a small jack plug. Used for playing phones or MP3 players through an old car stereo.

radio-presets.context: A radio with a tuning display above two rows of three preset buttons. Used for saved stations, favourite channels and quick tuning memory buttons.

movie-poster.context: A tall poster with a film strip band across the top and title lines at the bottom. Used for film posters, movie listings, promo art and cinema now showing displays.

age-rating.context: A rounded badge showing the number 7 with a plus sign beside it. Used for minimum age ratings, parental guidance labels and content suitability notices on films, games and shows.

outdoor-cinema.context: A large screen on two poles standing on grass and showing a play triangle. Used for open air film nights, garden cinemas and summer screenings.

capture-card.context: A small box with an HDMI style port on the left and a cable plugged in on the right. Used for game capture, streaming gear and recording video from consoles or cameras.

reaction-video.context: A video frame with a play triangle and a small round face bubble in the corner. Used for reaction videos, picture in picture commentary and facecam overlays.

dolly-track.context: A camera on a wheeled cart rolling along a straight rail. Used for smooth tracking shots, film set equipment and camera movement options.

loop-recording.context: A solid record dot sitting inside a circular arrow. Used for dash cams and security cameras that record continuously and overwrite the oldest footage.

voice-changer.context: A small microphone with a jagged wave that turns into a smooth wave. Used for pitch shifting, robot voices and voice effect settings in calls, games and recorders.

parametric-equalizer.context: A framed graph with a smooth curve that rises to one bell shaped peak and dips in a trough, each marked by a dot. Used for frequency band tuning, EQ settings and audio mastering.

car-infotainment.context: A car dashboard screen showing a small album square and a play triangle, with air vents on either side and a dash line below. Used for in car media, phone mirroring systems and head unit settings.

stadium-screen.context: A large screen raised on two legs above curved rows of stadium seats. Used for jumbotrons, scoreboards, replay screens and arena venue features.

music-charts.context: A ranked list of three rows with a music note on top and small up and down trend marks beside the rows. Used for top songs lists, hit parades and music popularity rankings.

concert-ticket.context: A ticket with notched sides, a perforation line and a music note on the main part. Used for gig and festival tickets, live music bookings and event passes.

portable-dvd-player.context: A clamshell player opened at an angle, with a play triangle on its screen and a disc and buttons on its base. Used for car and travel DVD players and disc based video.

cinema-camera.context: A boxy digital cinema camera with a top handle, a large lens and a rectangular matte box in front. Used for film production, professional shooting and camera rental topics.

burn-disc.context: A compact disc with a small flame rising from its upper right edge. Used for burning CDs and DVDs, writing data to disc and copy to disc actions.

optical-drive.context: A slim disc drive with its tray slid out holding a disc. Used for CD, DVD and Blu-ray drives, inserting or ejecting a disc and optical media settings.

merge-clips.context: Two short timeline clips with an arrow pointing down into one longer clip below. Used for joining, combining or concatenating video and audio clips in an editor.

lower-third.context: A video frame with a thick name bar and a thinner title bar across its lower left. Used for on screen names, captions and broadcast graphics in news and interviews.

cable-tv.context: A television set with a thick coaxial cable leaving its back and ending in a screw plug. Used for cable television service, coax connections and antenna cable setup.

cd-wallet.context: A zippered disc wallet opened flat with one disc in a sleeve on each page. Used for CD and DVD storage, car disc folders and media collections.

cd-spindle.context: A tall stack of discs on a central post with a domed lid lifted above. Used for blank CD or DVD packs, bulk disc storage and burning supplies.

sleep-sounds.context: A crescent moon with a music note and two gentle wave lines below. Used for lullabies, white noise, calming night playlists and bedtime audio settings.

album-carousel.context: A row of three album covers with the centre one facing forward and the side ones angled away, and page dots below. Used for cover flow style browsing in music libraries.

computer-speakers.context: A monitor on a desk flanked by two small upright speakers. Used for desktop audio settings, multimedia speakers and PC sound output.

shower-speaker.context: A round waterproof speaker hanging from a suction cup, with water droplets beside it. Used for bathroom music, splash proof Bluetooth speakers and shower playlists.

bone-conduction-headphones.context: A head in side view with a band curving around the ear and a pad resting in front of it. Used for open ear sport headphones that send sound through the cheekbones.

pay-per-view.context: A television screen with a coin dropping into its top edge and a play triangle on the screen. Used for paid events, rented movies and premium one off streams.

motion-capture.context: A standing figure with marker dots on its joints and a camera pointed at it. Used for mocap animation, tracking suits and performance capture in films and games.

photosensitivity-warning.context: A screen with a lightning bolt above a small eye. Used for flashing light and strobe warnings about seizure risk in videos, games and shows.

silent-disco.context: A dancing figure wearing large headphones with one arm raised. Used for headphone parties, silent club nights and festival listening events.

teletext.context: A television screen filled with blocky text rows and a three digit page number on top. Used for teletext services, text based TV news pages and retro broadcast information.

console-radiogram.context: A long low cabinet on tapered legs with a speaker on one half and a lift up lid over the turntable on the other. Used for mid century hi fi furniture and vintage stereo systems.

dialogue-enhancement.context: A speech bubble holding a tall sound wave above a flat background line. Used for clear speech and voice boost settings that raise dialogue over music and effects.

sports-broadcast.context: A television with an antenna showing a soccer ball and a small live dot in the corner. Used for live sports channels, match coverage and game day streams.

video-rental-store.context: A small shop front with a striped awning, a row of film strip holes above the door and a door below. Used for movie rental shops, video stores and retro film retail.

play-selection.context: A pair of square brackets enclosing a play triangle. Used for playing only a selected range, in and out points and looping a marked section.

karaoke-microphone.context: A handheld microphone with a wide round speaker style head and buttons on its handle. Used for karaoke, party singing and sing along features.

drive-in-speaker.context: A metal box speaker with a grille hanging on a hook over the top edge of a car window glass. Used for drive in cinema, retro film nights and car side audio.

surtitles.context: A theatre stage with open curtains and a long text bar above the stage opening. Used for opera and stage show captions and live translated text above the performance.

score-overlay.context: A video frame with a small two column score box in its top left corner and a play triangle. Used for live match scores, sports graphics and scoreboard overlays on video.

lock-screen-player.context: A phone with a clock bar at the top and a control row of previous, play and next triangles beneath it. Used for lock screen and notification media controls on phones.

volume-mixer.context: Three horizontal slider tracks, each with a small speaker on the left and a knob set at a different position. Used for per app volume and channel level mixing.

next-episode.context: A small thumbnail beside a ring that counts down around a play triangle. Used for autoplay up next prompts and binge watching in streaming apps.

audio-feedback.context: A microphone and a loudspeaker with a jagged squeal line running from one to the other. Used for howl and feedback problems in sound checks and PA systems.

group-listening.context: Two pairs of headphones side by side joined by a short link, with a music note above. Used for shared and synchronised listening sessions with friends.

thaumatrope.context: A round disc with a bird drawn on it, held by strings that fork out at both sides. Used for early optical toys, persistence of vision and the history of animation.

headphone-splitter.context: A Y shaped adapter with a jack plug at the base and two round sockets at the forked ends. Used for sharing one audio output between two headphones.

timeline-snap.context: A horseshoe magnet above a clip edge with a thin guide line running down to the clip. Used for magnetic snapping and aligning clips in video editors.

tangled-tape.context: A cassette with a loose loop of tape spilling out of it in tangled curls. Used for tape jams, damaged cassettes and retro audio problems.

video-glitch.context: A video frame holding a play triangle cut into horizontal slices that sit shifted sideways. Used for glitch effects, corrupted playback and broken stream errors.

hdmi-switch.context: A small box with three input ports on the left, one output port on the right and an arrow across the middle. Used for HDMI selectors, AV switches and choosing between video sources.

volume-buttons.context: The edge of a phone with two raised buttons and a plus and a minus sign beside them. Used for volume up and down hardware keys, button remapping and device help pages.

earbud-tap-control.context: A single earbud with a fingertip touching its outer face and ripple arcs showing the tap. Used for touch controls and gesture settings on wireless earbuds.

inline-remote.context: An earphone cable with a small oblong remote in the middle carrying three buttons. Used for wired headset controls, in line microphones and play, pause and volume clickers.
